firewall_empty_subtitle: Turn the firewall on in a location's settings, then add rules here. Traffic no rule matches follows the location's default.
firewall_delete_confirm_body: Delete rule **{name}**? Gateways stop enforcing it within a second.
firewall_save_success: Rule saved. Gateways are updated within a second.
firewall_section_sources_text: Traffic from the VPN addresses of these users' devices, groups' members' devices and network devices. Disabled users never match.
firewall_helper_action: Deny drops traffic silently; Reject also tells the sender, so apps fail fast.
firewall_helper_priority: Lower numbers are checked first. Rules with the same number keep their creation order.
firewall_helper_destinations: IP addresses, CIDR networks or ranges, separated by commas or new lines. Example: 10.0.0.5, 192.168.1.0/24, 10.1.0.1-10.1.0.50
firewall_helper_ports: Comma-separated, e.g. 443, 8000-8080. Empty means any port. Ports apply to TCP and UDP.
firewall_error_no_source: Choose who this rule applies to, or anyone on the VPN.
firewall_error_no_destination: Add at least one address, or choose anywhere.
firewall_error_no_location: Choose at least one location, or all locations.
firewall_snat_empty_subtitle: Make a user's VPN traffic leave a location's gateways with a fixed public address. The address must be configured on those gateways.
firewall_snat_helper_ip: IPv4 or IPv6 address configured on the location's gateways.
firewall_snat_delete_body: Traffic from this user will leave with the gateway's normal address again.
